licensure.disciplinary_grounds.rationale: These nine buckets capture the dominant clusters visible across all states: license/practice fraud and deception; criminal convictions; clinical quality failures (negligence, malpractice, incompetence); substance abuse and physical/mental impairment; controlled-substance and prescribing violations; sexual misconduct with patients; broad unprofessional/dishonorable conduct; failures to comply with board orders, reporting duties, and administrative requirements; and failures in supervising or delegating to subordinates.

profession_specific.license_status_types.rationale: These nine buckets capture the dominant structural distinctions in the data: standard unrestricted practice (active), non-practicing statuses (inactive/retired), time-limited credentials pending full licensure (temporary/provisional), credentials tied to postgraduate training programs (resident/training permits), scope-restricted or condition-bearing licenses (limited/restricted/conditional), academic/faculty roles (teaching/visiting professor), non-clinical administrative medicine, charitable volunteer practice, and multi-state or compact/extraterritorial credentials—together covering every observed item type without over-relying on a catch-all.
